title: What the Notes Left Behind
transcript: In a study skills class, students watched the same short talk about ocean currents. Half took notes by hand, and the rest typed on laptops with internet access turned off. The typed notes contained more details, including several phrases copied almost word for word. The handwritten notes were shorter and often grouped related ideas under a single heading. The next day, everyone took a quiz before seeing their notes again. Both groups did about equally well on factual items, but the handwriting group was better at explaining how two processes were connected. The instructor planned a further trial in which students would review their notes before the quiz.

questions.prompt: What difference did the instructor observe in the handwritten notes?
options: They were shorter and often organized related ideas together.
They contained more examples from the talk.
They followed the speaker's wording more closely.
They used more headings to separate individual details.
questions.answer: They were shorter and often organized related ideas together.
questions.explanation: 手写笔记篇幅较短，而且常把有关联的观点归在同一标题下。

questions.prompt: Where did the handwriting group have an advantage on the quiz?
options: Remembering individual facts about ocean currents
Recognizing phrases the speaker had used
Recalling the order in which examples appeared
Explaining the relationship between two processes
questions.answer: Explaining the relationship between two processes
questions.explanation: 两组在事实题上表现相近，手写组更擅长解释两个过程之间的关系。
